newsitem.title: FRANCE: French leftist sees Europe as election focus.
newsitem.headline: French leftist sees Europe as election focus.

text.p: French leftist Eurosceptic and former cabinet member Max Gallo said on Monday he would support a call by Gaullist President Jacques Chirac for snap elections but added that the Socialists needed to hone their message on European monetary union.
Gallo, a former Socialist who served as secretary of state and government spokesman in 1983-84, is now a member of the tiny Citizens Movement party.
"In the position in which we find ourselves in this mess, it seems that Chirac must announce a dissolution (of parliament)," Gallo told RMC Radio.

"I think the Left has set out a programme, I think we all know where we are headed -- that is, towards Maastricht -- and the French people should be allowed to express themselves on this question as soon as possible," Gallo said.
He said he was pleased that Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin's position on Europe had evolved but said Jospin "remained quite vague" on the issue.

Jospin said on Sunday that he opposed further austerity measures to assure France qualifies for a single currency, said that Italy and Spain should take part in the first wave of monetary union and proposed talks with France's partners to discuss under what conditions a single currency should go ahead.

Gallo said, "The question which arises is as follows: If the Germans say, 'We back the Maastricht criteria, we do not want Italy and Portugal', is the Left obliged to destroy this concept of Europe, or not. That is the only question," Gallo said.

"What I fear is that, if the French people feel they are told things simply because it is election time, that conditions are put on Europe which it is understood will not be respected, it is obvious that the French people will not vote for the Left but for something else," he said.
